newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies move sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies move sharply higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were limit up to sharply higher in late trading and pork belly futures were sharply higher amid active commodity fund short covering, traders said.
"There was a lot of short covering," said one trader.
Traders said higher-than-expected cash hog prices Friday prompted early local buying that lifted futures and activated chart-based buying.
Cash hogs traded mostly $0.50 to $1.50 per cwt higher Friday at Midwest markets, which was contrary to ideas late Thursday for steady to lower prices.
Buying in CME December hogs accelerated when chart-based buying developed after prices rose through technical resistance at 55.15 cents per lb, traders said.

At 1150 CDT, hogs were up 1.850 to 0.300 cent a lb with December up the 1.50 limit at 55.900 cents. About 105 contracts were bid limit up but unfilled. The daily limit in February 1997 and forward lean hog contracts is 2.00 cents.
Pork bellies were up 2.900 to 2.500 cents with February up 2.650 at 70.950 cents per lb.
